accordionPanel1Content: Nestled in the heart of Lovingston, Trager Brothers Coffee 1.0 boasts a unique charm that is deeply intertwined with the town's rich history. Among its notable historical claims to fame, the town prides itself on a jail that was designed by none other than Thomas Jefferson, showcasing the architectural brilliance of the Founding Father. Equally significant, the Bright Hope Baptist Church stands as a testament to the enduring spirit of the community. Built in 1870, this historic African-American landmark was established for the freedmen and women residing in Nelson, serving as a beacon of hope and unity in the post-Civil War era. Together, these landmarks encapsulate the deep historical roots from which Trager Brothers Coffee draws its inspiration, blending the rich past with the vibrant present of Lovingston.
accordionPanel2Content:
Nestled in the heart of Lovingston, the Trager Brothers Coffee 1.0 café finds itself in a location steeped in rich history and community spirit. Adjacent to this family-owned coffee haven is the Bright Hope Baptist Church, an iconic African-American landmark that commands a sweeping view over the village. This church, alongside a school built in the same era, was established in 1870 as a beacon of hope and education for the freed men and women of Nelson County. The meticulously maintained grounds surrounding the church hold over 100 marked graves, serving as a poignant reminder of the area's deep historical roots and the enduring strength of its community. 

Trager Brothers Coffee 1.0 prides itself on being an integral part of this vibrant local history. As a small-batch, entirely "a mano" (by hand) operation, the café embodies the artisan spirit that has long thrived in the region. Specializing in sight roasting to order, they ensure that no roasted coffee is warehoused, guaranteeing the freshest espresso pours and whole bean sales. This dedication to quality and community makes a visit to Trager Brothers Coffee 1.0 not just a simple coffee run, but a rich, immersive experience into the heart of Lovingston's heritage.

accordionPanel1Content: Nestled in the heart of Virginia, the charming historic village of Lovingstown began its story in 1809. Originating from a land grant, the need to establish both a courthouse and a county seat for the newly created Nelson County set the stage for Lovingstown's birth. It was in this pivotal year that James Loving laid down the foundation for what would become a quaint and picturesque village. The initial development saw 49 lots being meticulously parceled off in nearly equal measure, subsequently being sold to pave the way for the community's growth. This marked the beginning of Lovingstown's rich history, setting the stage for its evolution into the vibrant community it is today.
accordionPanel2Content:
Nestled within the heart of Lovingston, Chicken Coop offers a delightful culinary experience, tucked away inside the Nelson Food Mart Exxon. This quick-service comfort-food counter is renowned for its crispy fried chicken, smoked barbecue, burgers, and hearty sandwiches, accompanied by indulgent sides like mac and cheese. It's a gem for those in pursuit of satisfying, home-style cooking.

Just a stone's throw away from Chicken Coop, visitors can immerse themselves in the rich history of the area at Bright Hope Baptist Church. This historic African-American landmark, overlooking the quaint village of Lovingston, stands as a poignant reminder of the community's resilience and strength. Constructed in 1870 alongside a school, the church was established to serve the freed men and women of Nelson County in the aftermath of the Civil War. The well-preserved grounds are home to over 100 marked graves, offering a solemn and reflective space for visitors to pay their respects and learn more about the local history.

Whether you're drawn to the area by the allure of savory, comfort food at Chicken Coop or the historical significance of Bright Hope Baptist Church, Lovingston offers a rich tapestry of culinary and cultural experiences waiting to be explored.

accordionPanel1Content: Nestled within the breathtaking landscapes of Virginia, Wintergreen Resort holds the title of the region's largest tubing park, famously known as The Plunge. Picture yourself perched atop a structure as grand as a ten-story building, your gaze stretching out over the expansive hill that unfolds before you, extending beyond the length of three football fields. It's here, at The Plunge, where you can embark on an exhilarating journey downhill, racing through the crisp, winter air on a tube at thrilling speeds of up to 30 mph. This remarkable adventure has contributed to Wintergreen Resort's esteemed recognition, not once, but twice, as the "Best Ski Resort" by the readers of the Washington Post. Whether you're a seasoned snow enthusiast or seeking a unique winter thrill, The Plunge offers an unforgettable experience that captures the essence of outdoor excitement and the sheer joy of snow tubing.
accordionPanel2Content:
Nestled in a winter wonderland, twice crowned as the "Best Ski Resort" by the esteemed readers of the Washington Post, this destination offers more than just picturesque landscapes. It's a haven for both skiers and snowboarders alike, eager to perfect their freestyle maneuvers or perhaps, to take the first thrilling slide down the slopes. The Terrain Park, a highlight of this storied resort, is meticulously crafted to cater to a wide array of skill levels, from the novices taking their tentative first slides to the seasoned professionals carving the snow with precision.

As you glide into the Terrain Park, you'll be greeted by an ever-changing array of rails, each designed to test and enhance your skills. On any given day, the park may feature an assortment of rails including the whimsical rainbows, the straightforward straight rails, the challenging battle ships, the intricate down-kinks, the serpentine s-rails, and the playful fun boxes. Each piece is a puzzle, inviting you to unlock new skills and techniques.

But the innovation doesn't stop at metallic challenges. The Terrain Park also boasts a variety of snow features that morph the landscape into a freestyler's dream. You might find yourself airborne off a tabletop, navigating the complex curves of a spine, or mastering the transitions of a hip. These snow features are not just obstacles; they are canvases, allowing each rider and skier to paint their unique trail of twists, turns, and aerial feats.

In this award-winning ski resort, every visit to the Terrain Park is an opportunity to explore, to grow, and to be inspired. Whether you're drawn by the allure of the rails or the call of the snow features, your freestyle skills will find both challenge and refinement here. Come for the pristine snow and the accolades, but stay for the endless possibilities that await in the Terrain Park.

accordionPanel1Content:
Nestled in the heart of Virginia, Drumheller's Orchard stands as a testament to the rich history and vibrant culture of Lovingston. This family-owned orchard and bakery is not just renowned for its classic Virginia apple varieties, house cider, and delightful fall festivals complete with hayrides and an array of baked goods; it is also steeped in the locality's storied past. Lovingston itself boasts a unique claim to fame, having its town jail designed by the esteemed Thomas Jefferson, adding a touch of historical significance to the area's architectural landscape.

But Lovingston's historical allure doesn't end there. Among its most significant landmarks is the Bright Hope Baptist Church. Constructed in 1870, this church holds a special place in the hearts of the local community. It was built as a sanctuary for the freedmen and women residing in Nelson, marking a pivotal moment in the area's history. Today, it stands as Lovingston’s most historic African-American landmark, a poignant reminder of the town's journey towards freedom and equality.

Drumheller's Orchard, with its deep roots in this historical tapestry, offers more than just a taste of Virginia's famed apples and baked goods. It serves as a gateway to the past, inviting visitors to explore the rich heritage of Lovingston while enjoying the simple pleasures of orchard life. Whether you're here for the crisp apples, the homemade cider, or the warmth of the fall festivals, you'll find yourself immersed in a place where history and harvest intertwine beautifully.
accordionPanel2Content:
Discover the heart of Virginia's apple country at Drumheller's Orchard, a family-owned gem nestled in the picturesque landscape of Lovingston. This enchanting orchard and bakery is not just a place to pick apples; it's a celebration of Virginia's rich agricultural heritage, offering a selection of classic apple varieties, house-made cider, and a calendar filled with fall festivals that charm visitors of all ages. The grounds are pet-friendly, inviting you and your furry friends to explore the scenic beauty of the orchard. With hayrides weaving through the trees and the aroma of freshly baked goods filling the air, Drumheller's Orchard promises a delightful experience for every visitor.

Adding to the orchard's allure is its proximity to the Bright Hope Baptist Church, a historic African-American landmark with deep roots in the community. Overlooking the village of Lovingston, the church, alongside a school, was established in 1870, serving as a beacon of hope for the freed men and women of Nelson County. The surrounding area, meticulously kept, is home to over 100 marked graves, offering a solemn reminder of the past and a place for reflection amidst the natural beauty of Virginia. Drumheller's Orchard not only offers a taste of Virginia's finest apples but also a slice of its rich cultural history, making every visit a truly enriching experience.
accordionPanel3Content:

Not just a feast for the senses, Drumheller's Orchard also prides itself on its house cider, a testament to the craft and tradition that has been a pillar of the establishment.

But the experience at Drumheller's doesn't end with the taste of its harvest. The orchard transforms into a hub of joy and community during the fall, hosting festivals that promise more than just the delight of apple picking. Imagine taking a leisurely hayride through the scenic grounds, the laughter of loved ones mingling with the rustle of leaves underfoot. These festivals are a celebration of autumn, featuring an array of baked goods that epitomize the season's flavors, alongside the pet-friendly grounds that welcome all members of the family, ensuring that no one misses out on the fun.

The brewery is a haven for those who appreciate the art of craft beer, offering a selection of brews that capture the essence of the region, all while providing a plethora of outdoor activities that cater to every member of the family.

Drumheller's Orchard and its surroundings present a tapestry of experiences that weave together the beauty of Virginia's landscapes, the taste of its harvest, and the joy of community gatherings. It's a place where every visit is more than just a day out; it's an opportunity to create memories that linger, long after the last leaf of autumn has fallen.

name: Blue Ridge Tunnel
description: Walk the restored 1850s Blue Ridge Railroad tunnel on a 2.25-mile crushed-gravel path with dramatic stone portals linking Afton and the Rockfish Valley. The Blue Ridge Tunnel, engineered by Claudius Crozet in the 1850s beneath Rockfish Gap, now lets hikers and cyclists travel nearly a mile through the historic rail bore between Skyline Drive and the Blue Ridge Parkway.
image1Desc: Cyclist with headlight in dark tunnel, wet rocky walls.
amenities: Biking; Educational; Hiking; Parking; Scenic Views
accordionPanel1Content:
Nestled within the picturesque landscapes that bridge Afton and the Rockfish Valley, the Blue Ridge Tunnel stands as a testament to historical engineering and natural beauty. This 2.25-mile hike takes adventurers along a crushed-gravel path, through the heart of a restored 1850s Blue Ridge Railroad tunnel, and between its dramatic stone portals, crafting an atmosphere that's both awe-inspiring and serene.

The genius behind this architectural marvel was French immigrant Claudius Crozet (1789–1864), whose life and career were as remarkable as the tunnel itself. Crozet, a distinguished graduate from the prestigious École Polytechnique in Paris, had an illustrious career that saw him serving as an artillery officer during Napoleon’s harrowing invasion of Russia. His expertise and experiences didn't just end on the battlefield. Crozet went on to educate future engineers as a professor of engineering, imparting his vast knowledge and shaping the minds that would continue to build America.

But it's perhaps his role as the chief engineer of the Blue Ridge Tunnel that stands out amongst his numerous achievements. Under his guidance, the tunnel was carved through the mountains, a feat that not only showcased his unparalleled skills and vision but also his ability to overcome the formidable challenges posed by such a rugged landscape.

Today, the Blue Ridge Tunnel serves as a captivating journey through time, inviting visitors to walk the path that trains once traveled, surrounded by the enduring legacy of Claudius Crozet's work. It's an experience that combines the thrill of exploration with a deep appreciation for the history and natural beauty of the region, making it a must-visit for anyone seeking adventure and inspiration in the great outdoors.

The dramatic stone portals that mark the entrance and exit of the tunnel stand as a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of a bygone era.

Join us in honoring the past, delighting in the present, and preserving the future of the Blue Ridge Tunnel. Your journey through this remarkable passage is more than a walk—it's a step into history, an encounter with nature, and an adventure to be treasured.
accordionPanel3Content:

James Loving, an individual whose name is now synonymous with the village, took the lead in this ambitious project. With a vision for a thriving settlement, construction commenced, forever changing the landscape of what was once untouched nature. accordionPanel1Content:
Nestled in the heart of Schuyler, the Quarry Gardens at Schuyler stand as a testament to both human ingenuity and nature's resilience. These gardens were born from the remnants of soapstone quarries, which, after years of extraction and industry, have been lovingly restored into a breathtaking 40-acre expanse. Today, visitors can wander through native plant gardens beautifully integrated into the landscape, explore two miles of trails that meander through diverse habitat galleries, and participate in guided ecology tours that offer insight into the area's natural and cultural history.

The story of the Quarry Gardens is deeply interwoven with the narrative of the Great Depression, a time when the demand for soapstone, and the labor to extract it, reached a peak in Schuyler. It's a history that speaks to the resilience of the community and the land itself, both of which have undergone tremendous transformation. From a bustling center of industry to a serene natural haven, the Quarry Gardens have emerged as a symbol of renewal and ecological stewardship.

Visitors to Schuyler are also encouraged to visit The Walton’s Mountain Museum, which offers another layer of local history and nostalgia, especially for those who remember or wish to discover the beloved television series that depicted rural Virginian life during the Great Depression.

The Quarry Gardens at Schuyler are more than just a destination; they are a journey through time, a celebration of nature's ability to heal and flourish, and an invitation to explore the delicate balance between past and present. Whether you're a history enthusiast, a nature lover, or simply in search of a peaceful retreat, the Quarry Gardens offer an experience that is as enriching as it is beautiful.
accordionPanel2Content:
Nestled within the heart of the region, the Quarry Gardens at Schuyler stand as a testament to nature's resilience and human innovation. This unique destination has transformed the remnants of soapstone quarries into a sprawling 40-acre sanctuary, featuring native plant gardens, two miles of meandering trails, habitat galleries, and the opportunity for guests to immerse themselves in guided ecology tours.

The history and background of this enchanting place are richly displayed at the Oakland Museum, where visitors can delve into an exhibit dedicated to The Rural Electrification Act—a pivotal part of Roosevelt's New Deal. This exhibit not only sheds light on a crucial piece of American history but also connects the dots to the local area's development and its role in the broader narrative of rural electrification.

Moreover, the museum offers a fascinating glimpse into the educational heritage of the area through an exhibit that showcases the evolution of schools and the impact of traveling teachers. This particular exhibit resonates deeply with both educators and students, offering them a chance to reflect on the history of schooling in rural settings and its transformative effects on communities.

The Quarry Gardens at Schuyler are more than just a beautiful escape; they are a bridge to the past, inviting visitors to explore the natural beauty that has been carefully preserved and the rich history that has shaped the region. It's a place where the past and present converge, offering a serene yet enlightening experience to all who wander its paths.

The Quarry Gardens, a 40-acre expanse meticulously restored from soapstone quarries, offer an enchanting blend of natural beauty and serene garden spaces. With two miles of trails winding through native plant gardens and habitat galleries, the area serves as a living showcase of ecological restoration and conservation.

The crisp mornings of fall, coupled with pleasant daytime temperatures and the hint of a chill as the sun sets, create an idyllic outdoor setting that's hard to resist. Whether you're meandering along the trails, immersed in the guided ecology tours, or simply soaking in the serene beauty of the gardens, the Quarry Gardens at Schuyler promise an experience that's as educational as it is aesthetically pleasing.

Beyond the allure of the outdoors, Nelson County and the Quarry Gardens offer a variety of cozy indoor amenities, ensuring that your visit is comfortable and rewarding, regardless of the weather. From the moment you arrive, you'll find yourself drawn into a world where nature and nurture seamlessly blend, offering a tranquil retreat from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. accordionPanel1Content: Nestled in the heart of Virginia, the quaint and historic village of Lovingstown began its story in 1809, born from a land grant and the pressing need to establish a courthouse, along with a county seat for the newly minted Nelson County. It was in that same year that James Loving laid the foundation for what would become a charming testament to early American resilience and community spirit. This picturesque village was meticulously planned, with 49 lots being carefully parceled out, each nearly equal in measure, and then sold to eager settlers. The result was a harmonious blend of structure and spontaneity, creating a legacy that continues to enchant visitors to this day. Lovingstown not only serves as a beacon of history but also as a gateway to the Nelson 29 craft beverage route, which weaves between Arrington and Faber, connecting 29 breweries, wineries, and distilleries along the scenic U.S. route. This unique trail highlights the rich agricultural and entrepreneurial spirit of Virginia, making Lovingstown a must-visit destination for those who appreciate the finer things in life, including a deep appreciation for history and a good drink in hand.
accordionPanel2Content:
Nestled within the picturesque landscape between Arrington and Faber lies the Nelson 29, a craft beverage route that caters not only to the palate of those who appreciate fine brews, wines, and spirits but also to those who seek a journey through history and culture. Along this route, one cannot miss the opportunity to visit the Bright Hope Baptist Church, an iconic historic African-American landmark situated in the heart of Lovingston.

This revered site, which majestically overlooks the village, is more than just a place of worship. Built in 1870, the Bright Hope Baptist Church, along with an adjoining school, was established to serve the freed men and women of Nelson County in the aftermath of the Civil War. This initiative was a beacon of hope and a testament to resilience, symbolizing a new chapter for the African-American community in the area.

The church grounds are a solemn reminder of the past, with over 100 marked graves that tell stories of the lives that shaped the community. Each gravestone serves as a marker of history, honoring the individuals who walked the paths of Nelson County and contributed to its rich cultural tapestry.

Visitors to the Nelson 29 craft beverage route are invited to take a moment to explore the Bright Hope Baptist Church and its surrounding area. It's an opportunity to reflect on the journey of a community through time while enjoying the scenic views that overlook the village of Lovingston. This landmark is not just a stop along a route; it's a bridge to the past, offering insights and a deeper appreciation for the journey ahead.
accordionPanel3Content:

name: Walton's Mountain Museum
description: The Walton’s Mountain Museum showcases the television show of the 1960s, “The Waltons”. Earl Hamner, Jr., creator of The Walton’s, grew up in Schuyler and many of the scripts were based on life as a boy in Schuyler, VA. The museum displays replicas of rooms on the TV show, such as John-Boy’s Bedroom, Ike Godsey’s Store, the kitchen and living room.
image1Desc: Brick building labeled 'Walton's Mountain Museum' with nearby sign, trees, and sunlight.
amenities: Retail; Seasonal Menu; Museum
accordionPanel1Content:
Nestled in the heart of Schuyler, the Walton's Mountain Museum stands as a beacon for enthusiasts of the cherished 1960s television show, "The Waltons." The museum is dedicated to preserving the essence and heartwarming narrative of this iconic series, which was brought to life by the creative genius of Earl Hamner, Jr. Born and raised in Schuyler, Hamner infused the show with the rich tapestry of his own experiences, setting many of the beloved scripts against the stark yet resilient backdrop of life during the Great Depression.

The museum not only serves as a tribute to the enduring legacy of "The Waltons" but also offers visitors a deep dive into the cultural and historical context of the era that inspired the series. For those journeying to Schuyler, a visit to the Walton's Mountain Museum is not just encouraged—it's considered a must for anyone looking to connect with the spirit of a bygone era that continues to resonate with audiences today. Through its carefully curated exhibits and memorabilia, the museum invites guests into the world of the Walton family, offering a unique glimpse into the struggles and triumphs of American life during one of its most challenging periods.
accordionPanel2Content:
Nestled within the welcoming confines of the Walton's Mountain Museum, visitors are treated to a fascinating journey back in time, exploring the rich tapestry of 1960s America through the lens of the beloved television show, "The Waltons". The museum, a tribute to the show's creator, Earl Hamner, Jr., offers a unique glimpse into the life and times of Schuyler, where Hamner grew up and drew inspiration for many of the show's heartfelt scripts.

Among the museum's highlights, the exhibit on The Rural Electrification Act stands out, offering an insightful look into one of the cornerstone policies of Roosevelt's New Deal. This pivotal piece of legislation, aimed at illuminating rural America, not only revolutionized the landscape of the country but also serves as a testament to the resilience and innovation of the era. The exhibit meticulously details the Act's profound impact on rural communities, weaving together historical narratives with interactive displays that bring the story to life.

Further enriching the museum's offerings is an exhibit dedicated to the history of the area's schools. This particular display is a treasure trove for traveling teachers and students alike, offering a captivating exploration of educational developments over the years. Through a series of engaging panels and artifacts, visitors can trace the evolution of schooling in the region, from one-room schoolhouses to the modern classrooms of today.

The Walton's Mountain Museum succeeds in not only preserving the legacy of a beloved American television show but also in capturing the essence of a bygone era. It stands as a testament to the power of storytelling, the importance of education, and the transformative impact of policy on the fabric of American life. As visitors meander through the exhibits, they are invited to reflect on the past, ponder the present, and imagine the future, all within the walls of this remarkable institution.
accordionPanel3Content:
Nestled in Nelson County, the fall season brings a spectacular transformation as the Blue Ridge Mountains don a breathtaking palette of autumn colors. The vibrancy of these hues reaches its zenith from mid- to late October, drawing visitors from near and far. The allure of fall in Nelson County is not just confined to its visual splendor; the season is characterized by crisp mornings that gently give way to pleasant daytime temperatures, before the day concludes with a nearly-chilly embrace. This climatic harmony creates an idyllic setting for outdoor adventures, ensuring that every moment spent in the embrace of nature is nothing short of magical.

However, the charm of Nelson County extends beyond its natural beauty. For those seeking refuge from the brisk outdoor air, the county offers a myriad of cozy indoor amenities. Among these, the Walton's Mountain Museum stands out as a beacon of cultural and historical significance. Celebrating the iconic 1960s television show, "The Waltons," the museum invites visitors into the world created by Earl Hamner, Jr. Having grown up in Schuyler, Hamner's own life and experiences heavily inspired the beloved series, with many of the scripts drawing directly from his memories of life in the area.

Visiting the Walton's Mountain Museum is not just a journey through a picturesque landscape; it is an immersive experience into a beloved piece of American television history, set against the backdrop of Nelson County's enchanting seasonal canvas.
